http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_289.label: ammonium
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_289.definition: An onium cation obtained by protonation of ammonia.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_138.label: gas molecular entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_138.definition: Any main group molecular entity that is gaseous at standard temperature and pressure (STP; 0°C and 100 kPa).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_252.label: metabolite
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_252.definition: Any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism. The term 'metabolite' subsumes the classes commonly known as primary and secondary metabolites.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_351.label: azane
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_351.definition: Saturated acyclic nitrogen hydrides having the general formula NnHn+2.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_161.label: ammonia
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_161.definition: An azane that consists of a single nitrogen atom covelently bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_253.label: monocarboxylic acid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_253.definition: An oxoacid containing a single carboxy group.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_378.label: plant hormone
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_378.definition: A plant growth regulator that modulates the formation of stems, leaves and flowers, as well as the development and ripening of fruit. The term includes endogenous and non-endogenous compounds (e.g. active compounds produced by bacteria on the leaf surface) as well as semi-synthetic and fully synthetic compounds.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_248.label: indole-3-acetic acids
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_248.definition: An  indol-3-yl carboxylic acid in which the carboxylic acid specified is acetic acid.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_226.label: auxin
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_226.definition: Any of a group of compounds, both naturally occurring and synthetic, that induce cell elongation in plant stems (from Greek αυξανω, "to grow").

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_769.label: plant metabolite
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_769.definition: Any eukaryotic metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in plants, the kingdom that include flowering plants, conifers and other gymnosperms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_164.label: indole-3-acetic acid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_164.definition: A monocarboxylic acid that is acetic acid in which one of the methyl hydrogens has been replaced by a 1H-indol-3-yl group.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_166.label: carbohydrate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_166.definition: Any member of the class of organooxygen compounds that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone or a lactol resulting from their intramolecular condensation (monosaccharides); substances derived from these by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by a hydrogen atom; and polymeric products arising by intermolecular acetal formation between two or more such molecules (disaccharides, polysaccharides and oligosaccharides). Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen atoms; prior to any oxidation or reduction, most have the empirical formula Cm(H2O)n. Compounds obtained from carbohydrates by substitution, etc., are known as carbohydrate derivatives and may contain other elements. Cyclitols are generally not regarded as carbohydrates.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_786.label: carbohydrates and carbohydrate derivatives
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_786.definition: Any organooxygen compound that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone, or a compound derived from one. Carbohydrates contain only carbon, hydrogen and oxygen and usually have an empirical formula Cm(H2O)n; carbohydrate derivatives may contain other elements by substitution or condensation.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_627.label: reactive nitrogen species
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_627.definition: A family of nitrogen molecular entities which are highly reactive and derived from nitric oxide (•NO) and superoxide (O<small><sub>2</sub></small>•<small><sup>−</small></sup>) produced via the enzymatic activity of inducible nitric oxide synthase 2 (NOS2) and NADPH oxidase respectively.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_176.label: nitrate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_176.definition: A nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitric acid. Principal species present at pH 7.3.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.label: monovalent inorganic anion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.definition: Any inorganic anion with a valency of one.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_244.label: glycosyl glycoside
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_244.definition: Any disaccharide in which the two monosaccharide components are connected by a glycosidic linkage between their anomeric centres.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_179.label: sucrose
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_179.definition: A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_183.label: phosphate(3-)
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_183.definition: A phosphate ion that is the conjugate base of hydrogenphosphate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_357.label: phosphate ion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_357.definition: A phosphorus oxoanion that is the conjugate base of phosphoric acid.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.label: trivalent inorganic anion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.definition: Any inorganic anion with a valency of three.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_434.label: hydrogenphosphate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_434.definition: A phosphate ion that is the conjugate base of dihydrogenphosphate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_522.label: biochemical role
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_522.definition: A biological role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biochemical context.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.label: pnictogen
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.definition: Any p-block element atom that is in group 15 of the periodic table: nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_339.label: macronutrient
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_339.definition: Any nutrient required in large quantities by organisms throughout their life in order to orchestrate a range of physiological functions. Macronutrients are usually chemical elements (carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus and sulfur) that humans consume in the largest quantities. Calcium, sodium, magnesium and potassium are sometimes included as macronutrients because they are required in relatively large quantities compared with other vitamins and minerals.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: heteroorganic entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: A heteroorganic entity is an organic molecular entity in which carbon atoms or organic groups are bonded directly to one or more heteroatoms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_257.label: organophosphorus compound
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_257.definition: An organophosphorus compound is formally a compound containing at least one carbon-phosphorus bond, but the term is often extended to include esters and thioesters.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_260.label: phosphate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_260.definition: Salts and esters of phosphoric and oligophosphoric acids and their chalcogen analogues. In inorganic chemistry, the term is also used to describe anionic coordination entities with phosphorus as central atom.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_397.label: dihydrogenphosphate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_397.definition: A monovalent inorganic anion that consists of phosphoric acid in which one of the three OH groups has been deprotonated.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: fertilizer
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: A fertilizer is any substance that is added to soil or water to assist the growth of plants.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_260.label: phosphoric acid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_260.definition: A phosphorus oxoacid that consists of one oxo and three hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central phosphorus atom.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_596.label: phosphoric acids
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_596.definition: Compounds containing one or more phosphoric acid units.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_371.label: glucan
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_371.definition: A polysaccharide composed of glucose residues.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_280.label: amylopectin
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_280.definition: A polydisperse highly branched polysaccharide derivative composed of chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The chains are joined together by α(1→6) glycosidic linkages. A small number of α(1→3) glycosidic linkages and some 6-phosphate ester groups also may occur. The branches in amylopectin typically contain 24 to 30 glucose residues.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_280.label: starch
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_280.definition: The most important reserve polysaccharide found in plants. It is a glucan consisting of amylose and amylopectin.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_281.label: amylose
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_281.definition: A glucan composed of unbranched chains of <small>D</small>-glucopyranose residues in α(1→4) glycosidic linkage. The number of repeated glucose subunits (n) is usually in the range of 300 to 3000, but can be many thousands. One of the two components of starch (the other, 70-80%, being amylopectin). Cf. linear maltodextrin, in which the chain length is typically between 3 and 17 glucose units.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_652.label: polysaccharide derivative
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_652.definition: A carbohydrate derivative that is any derivative of a polysaccharide.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_503.label: onium cation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_503.definition: Mononuclear cations derived by addition of a hydron to a mononuclear parent hydride of the pnictogen, chalcogen and halogen families.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_602.label: monovalent inorganic cation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_602.definition: An atom or small molecule with a positive charge that does not contain carbon in covalent linkage, with a valency of one.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_291.label: potassium(1+)
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_291.definition: A monoatomic monocation obtained from potassium.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: nutrient
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: A nutrient is a food component that an organism uses to survive and grow.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_782.label: food component
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_782.definition: A physiological role played by any substance that is distributed in foodstuffs. It includes materials derived from plants or animals, such as vitamins or minerals, as well as environmental contaminants.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: agrochemical
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: An agrochemical is a substance that is used in agriculture or horticulture.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_360.label: protein
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_360.definition: A biological macromolecule minimally consisting of one polypeptide chain synthesized at the ribosome.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_246.label: hormone
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_246.definition: Originally referring to an endogenous compound that is formed in specialized organ or group of cells and carried to another organ or group of cells, in the same organism, upon which it has a specific regulatory function, the term is now commonly used to include non-endogenous, semi-synthetic and fully synthetic analogues of such compounds.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_261.label: plant growth regulator
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_261.definition: A chemical, natural or artificial, that can affect the rate of growth of a plant.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.label: divalent inorganic anion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_793.definition: Any inorganic anion with a valency of two.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_757.label: eukaryotic metabolite
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_757.definition: Any  metabolite produced during a metabolic reaction in eukaryotes, the taxon that include members of the fungi, plantae and animalia kingdoms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: organic material
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: Environmental material derived from living organisms and composed primarily of one or more biomacromolecules.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: astronomical body part
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: A material part of an astronomical body.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0610.label: water-holding capacity of soil
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0610.definition: Water-holding capacity which inheres in some soil.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0001.label: environmental material
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0001.definition: A material entity which other material entities in an environmental system are primarily or partially composed of.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: silt
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: Particulate environmental material which is primarily composed of silt particles.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.label: clay
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.definition: Particulate environmental material which 1) is composed primarily of clay particles, with only minor proportions of other materials, 2) demonstrates plasticity when wet, and 3) is capable of hardening when dried or fired.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: sand
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: Particulate environmental material which is composed primarily of particles of sand with only minor proportions of other substances.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.label: soil
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.definition: An environmental material which is primarily composed of minerals, varying proportions of sand, silt, and clay, organic material such as humus, interstitial gases, liquids, and a broad range of resident micro- and macroorganisms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: particulate environmental material
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: An environmental material which is composed primarily of particles.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.label: fertilized soil
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.definition: Soil which has been amended with fertilizers.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_10000.label: microbial community
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_10000.definition: An ecological community which is composed of co-existing populations of microbial organisms that interact, directly or indirectly, such that they impact one another's ecological fitness.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002502.label: root system
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002502.definition: A collective plant organ structure (PO:0025007) that produces root meristems (PO:0006085), the plant structures (PO:0009011) that arise from them and the parts thereof.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.label: rhizosphere
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0000.definition: The narrow region of soil that is directly influenced by root secretions and associated soil microorganisms.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: ecosystem
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: An environmental system which includes both living and non-living components.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: material entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: An independent continuant that is spatially extended whose identity is independent of that of other entities and can be maintained through time.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_336.label: biomacromolecule
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_336.definition: A macromolecule formed by a living organism.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: rhizosphere environment
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: An environmental system determined by the presence of a plant rhizosphere.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: environmental system
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: A system which has the disposition to environ one or more material entities.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.label: water-holding capacity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0100.definition: A disposition of a material entity which is realised when it is saturated with liquid water.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: concentration of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A quality inhering in a substance by virtue of the amount of the bearer's there is mixed with another substance.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0900.label: concentration of soil organic matter in soil
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_0900.definition: The concentration of a soil organic matter when measured in soil.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: acidity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A concentration quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing acid (hydrogen ions).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000399.label: acid phosphatase activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000399.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: an orthophosphoric monoester + H2O = an alcohol + phosphate, with an acid pH optimum.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001679.label: phosphatase activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001679.definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of a phosphoric monoester, releasing a phosphate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001529.label: secondary active transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001529.definition: Enables the transfer of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other, up its concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction and is driven by a chemiosmotic source of energy, not direct ATP coupling. Secondary active transporters include symporters and antiporters.
narrow_synonyms: energizer of outer membrane receptor-mediated transport activity

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000531.label: phosphate transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000531.definition: Enables the transfer of phosphate ions from one side of a membrane to the other, up its concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction and is driven by a chemiosmotic source of energy. Secondary active transporters include symporters and antiporters.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005123.label: establishment of localization
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005123.definition: Any process that localizes a substance or cellular component. This may occur via movement, tethering or selective degradation.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.label: transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.definition: The directed movement of substances (such as macromolecules, small molecules, ions) or cellular components (such as complexes and organelles) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, or within a multicellular organism by means of some agent such as a transporter or a transporter complex, a pore or a motor protein.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003000.label: metal ion transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003000.definition: The directed movement of metal ions, any metal ion with an electric charge, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.label: potassium ion transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.definition: The directed movement of potassium ions (K+) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.
related_synonyms: low voltage-dependent potassium channel auxiliary protein activity
low voltage-gated potassium channel auxiliary protein activity

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001569.label: inorganic anion transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001569.definition: The directed movement of inorganic anions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Inorganic anions are atoms or small molecules with a negative charge which do not contain carbon in covalent linkage.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.label: phosphate ion transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.definition: The directed movement of phosphate ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004356.label: cellular response to nitrogen levels
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004356.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of inorganic nitrogen.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000926.label: cellular response to starvation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000926.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of nourishment.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000699.label: cellular response to nitrogen starvation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000699.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of nitrogen.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000851.label: ammonium channel activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000851.definition: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of ammonium through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001526.label: channel activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001526.definition: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a solute through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel. Stereospecificity is not exhibited but this transport may be specific for a particular molecular species or class of molecules.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007248.label: ammonium transmembrane transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007248.definition: The process in which ammonium is transported across a membrane. Ammonium is the cation NH4+.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000864.label: carbohydrate transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000864.definition: The directed movement of carbohydrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Carbohydrates are a group of organic compounds based of the general formula Cx(H2O)y.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000968.label: indoleacetic acid biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000968.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of indole-3-acetic acid, a compound which functions as a growth regulator in plants.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004243.label: indole-containing compound biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004243.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of compounds that contain an indole (2,3-benzopyrrole) skeleton.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007233.label: monocarboxylic acid biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007233.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of monocarboxylic acids, any organic acid containing one carboxyl (-COOH) group.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000985.label: auxin biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000985.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of auxins, plant hormones that regulate aspects of plant growth.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000992.label: auxin polar transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000992.definition: The unidirectional movement of auxin in the stem from tip to base along the vector of gravity or basipetally.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_006091.label: auxin transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_006091.definition: The directed movement of auxin into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Auxins are a group of plant hormones that regulates aspects of plant growth.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004836.label: shoot system development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004836.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the shoot system over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001001.label: shoot system morphogenesis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001001.definition: The process in which the anatomical structures of the shoot are generated and organized. The shoot is the part of a seed plant body that is usually above ground.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000965.label: anatomical structure morphogenesis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000965.definition: The process in which anatomical structures are generated and organized. Morphogenesis pertains to the creation of form.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190170.label: response to oxygen-containing compound
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190170.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an oxygen-containing compound stimulus.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190169.label: response to nitrogen compound
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190169.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitrogen compound stimulus.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001016.label: response to nitrate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001016.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a nitrate stimulus.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004836.label: root development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004836.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the root over time, from its formation to the mature structure. The root is the water- and mineral-absorbing part of a plant which is usually underground, does not bear leaves, tends to grow downwards and is typically derived from the radicle of the embryo.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003526.label: meristem growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003526.definition: The increase in size or mass of a meristem, a region of tissue in a plant that is composed of one or more undifferentiated cells capable of undergoing mitosis and differentiation.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001044.label: root meristem growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001044.definition: The increase in size or mass of a root meristem, a population of undifferentiated cells in a plant root which maintains a continuous balance between the production of stem cells and the incorporation of their derivatives into the growth of the root.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001046.label: gene expression
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001046.definition: The process in which a gene's sequence is converted into a mature gene product (protein or RNA). This includes the production of an RNA transcript and its processing, as well as translation and maturation for protein-coding genes.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000905.label: macromolecule biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000905.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of a macromolecule, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001096.label: regulation of phosphate transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001096.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of phosphate transport. Phosphate transport is the directed movement of phosphate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005104.label: regulation of transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005104.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the directed movement of substances (such as macromolecules, small molecules, ions) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002285.label: transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002285.definition: Enables the transfer of a substance, usually a specific substance or a group of related substances, from one side of a membrane to the other.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001511.label: nitrate transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001511.definition: Enables the transfer of nitrate ions (NO3-) from one side of a membrane to the other.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001570.label: nitrate transmembrane transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001570.definition: The directed movement of nitrate into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001541.label: ATPase-coupled phosphate ion transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001541.definition: Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: ATP + H2O + phosphate(out) = ADP + phosphate + phosphate(in).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004262.label: ATPase-coupled transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004262.definition: Primary active transporter of a solute across a membrane, via the reaction: ATP + H2O = ADP + phosphate, to directly drive the transport of a substance across a membrane. The transport protein may be transiently phosphorylated (P-type transporters), or not (ABC-type transporters and other families of transporters). Primary active transport occurs up the solute's concentration gradient and is driven by a primary energy source.
exact_synonyms: ATPase activity, coupled to transmembrane movement of substances
broad_synonyms: ATPase activity, coupled to movement of substances
narrow_synonyms: hydrolase activity, acting on acid anhydrides, catalyzing transmembrane movement of substances

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005508.label: transmembrane transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005508.definition: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190202.label: nitrate import
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190202.definition: The directed movement of nitrate into a cell or organelle.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001576.label: disaccharide transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001576.definition: The directed movement of disaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Disaccharides are sugars composed of two monosaccharide units.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001577.label: sucrose transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001577.definition: The directed movement of sucrose into, out of or within a cell, or between cells by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Sucrose is the disaccharide fructofuranosyl-glucopyranoside.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000815.label: metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000815.definition: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism transforms chemical substances. This includes including anabolism (biosynthetic process) and catabolism (catabolic process). Metabolic processes includes the transformation of small molecules, as well  macromolecular processes such as DNA repair and replication, protein synthesis and degradation.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001597.label: carbon fixation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001597.definition: A metabolic process in which carbon (usually derived from carbon dioxide) is incorporated into organic compounds (usually carbohydrates).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001603.label: cellular response to phosphate starvation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001603.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of deprivation of phosphate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004257.label: phosphoric ester hydrolase activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004257.definition: Catalysis of the reaction: RPO-R' + H2O = RPOOH + R'H. This reaction is the hydrolysis of any phosphoric ester bond, any ester formed from orthophosphoric acid, O=P(OH)3.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004873.label: system development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004873.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of an organismal system over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A system is a regularly interacting or interdependent group of organs or tissues that work together to carry out a given biological process.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002262.label: root system development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002262.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the root system over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_016010.label: plant gross anatomical part developmental process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_016010.definition: A developmental process whose specific outcome is the progression of a gross anatomical part of a plant over time from an initial condition to a later condition.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005089.label: response to stimulus
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005089.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus. The process begins with detection of the stimulus and ends with a change in state or activity or the cell or organism.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003166.label: response to nutrient levels
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003166.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of nutrients.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003561.label: root hair
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003561.definition: A long, thin projection from a root epidermal cell that contains F-actin and tubulin, and a cell wall.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_012002.label: plasma membrane bounded cell projection
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_012002.definition: A prolongation or process extending from a cell and that is bounded by plasma membrane, e.g. a cilium, lamellipodium, or axon.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004000.label: growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004000.definition: The increase in size or mass of an entire organism, a part of an organism or a cell.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000815.label: biological_process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000815.definition: A biological process is the execution of a genetically-encoded biological module or program. It consists of all the steps required to achieve the specific biological objective of the module. A biological process is accomplished by a particular set of molecular functions carried out by specific gene products (or macromolecular complexes), often in a highly regulated manner and in a particular temporal sequence.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007194.label: nitrogen cycle metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007194.definition: A nitrogen compound metabolic process that contributes to the nitrogen cycle. The nitrogen cycle is a series of metabolic pathways by which nitrogen is converted between various forms and redox states; it encompasses pathways in which nitrogen is acted upon directly, such as nitrification, denitrification, nitrogen fixation, and mineralization.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004212.label: nitrate metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004212.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving nitrates, inorganic or organic salts and esters of nitric acid.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004212.label: nitrate assimilation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004212.definition: The nitrogen metabolic process that encompasses the uptake of nitrate from the environment and reduction to ammonia, and results in the incorporation of nitrogen derived from nitrate into cellular substances.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004440.label: biological process involved in symbiotic interaction
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004440.definition: A process carried out by gene products in an organism that enable the organism to engage in a symbiotic relationship, a more or less intimate association, with another organism. The various forms of symbiosis include parasitism, in which the association is disadvantageous or destructive to one of the organisms; mutualism, in which the association is advantageous, or often necessary to one or both and not harmful to either; and commensalism, in which one member of the association benefits while the other is not affected. However, mutualism, parasitism, and commensalism are often not discrete categories of interactions and should rather be perceived as a continuum of interaction ranging from parasitism to mutualism. In fact, the direction of a symbiotic interaction can change during the lifetime of the symbionts due to developmental changes as well as changes in the biotic/abiotic environment in which the interaction occurs. Microscopic symbionts are often referred to as endosymbionts.
related_synonyms: symbiotic interaction between host and organism

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004441.label: biological process involved in interspecies interaction between organisms
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004441.definition: Any process evolved to enable an interaction with an organism of a different species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009940.label: plant organ development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009940.definition: Development of a plant organ, a multi-tissue plant structure that forms a functional unit.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004852.label: post-embryonic root development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004852.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the post-embryonic root over time, from its formation to the mature structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004852.label: lateral root development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004852.definition: The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the lateral root over time, from its formation to the mature structure. A lateral root is one formed from pericycle cells located on the xylem radius of the root, as opposed to the initiation of the main root from the embryo proper.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004876.label: root hair elongation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004876.definition: The process in which the root hair grows longer.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004858.label: developmental cell growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004858.definition: The growth of a cell, where growth contributes to the progression of the cell over time from one condition to another.
exact_synonyms: developmental growth of a unicellular organism

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_006056.label: developmental growth involved in morphogenesis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_006056.definition: The increase in size or mass of an anatomical structure that contributes to the structure attaining its shape.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009877.label: inorganic ion homeostasis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009877.definition: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of inorganic ions within an organism or cell.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005506.label: phosphate ion homeostasis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005506.definition: Any process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of phosphate ions within an organism or cell.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000998.label: cellular process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000998.definition: Any process that is carried out at the cellular level, but not necessarily restricted to a single cell. For example, cell communication occurs among more than one cell, but occurs at the cellular level.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007170.label: nitrogen compound transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_007170.definition: The directed movement of nitrogen-containing compounds into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009054.label: response to nitrate starvation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009054.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a starvation stimulus, deprivation of nitrate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004259.label: response to starvation
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004259.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a starvation stimulus, deprivation of nourishment.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_011006.label: ammonium transmembrane transporter complex
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_011006.definition: High affinity ammonium transporter complex that enables the transfer of ammonium from one side of a membrane to the other.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190249.label: transmembrane transporter complex
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_190249.definition: A transmembrane protein complex which enables the transfer of a substance from one side of a membrane to the other.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: amount
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: The number of entities of this type that are part of the whole organism.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: has number of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: The number of parts of a particular type that the bearer entity has. This is a relational quality, and thus holds between two entities: the bearer of the quality, and the type of parts.
exact_synonyms: extra or missing physical or functional parts
has or lacks parts of type

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: physical object characteristic
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A characteristic which inheres in a continuant.
exact_synonyms: multiply inhering quality of a physical entity
quality of a single physical entity

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: morphology
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A characterisitic of a single physical entity inhering in the bearer by virtue of the bearer's size or shape or structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: size
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's physical magnitude.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: 1-D extent
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A size quality inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's extension in one dimension.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: length
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A 1-D extent quality which is equal to the distance between two points.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: mass
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A physical quality that inheres in a bearer by virtue of the proportion of the bearer's amount of matter.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A morphology quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's relative position, shape, arrangements and connectivity of an organism's various parts; the pattern underlying its form.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: thickness
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A 1-D extent quality which is equal to the dimension through an object as opposed to its length or width.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: volume
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A 3-D extent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's amount of 3-dimensional space it occupies.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: 3-D extent
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A size quality inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's extension in three dimensions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: 2-D extent
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A size quality inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's extension in two dimensions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: area
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A 2-D extent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's two dimensional extent.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: ratio
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's magnitude in proportion to the magnitude of another entity.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.label: multi-species collection of microbes
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.definition: A multi-species collection of organisms that consists of two or more microbes from at least two species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.label: ecological community
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.definition: A multi-species collection of organisms of at least two different species, living in a particular area. Must have at least two populations of different species as members.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.label: plant exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.definition: A plant experimental condition (PECO:0007359) or set of conditions describing the application of an abiotic (PECO:0007191) or biotic plant exposure (PECO:0007357) or the combinatorial application thereof.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: plant experimental condition
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant exposure (PECO:0001001) and/or study condition (PECO:0007231) applied to a whole plant (PO:0000003), a plant structure (PO:00090119), and/or a plant population.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: plant macronutrient exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant nutrient exposure (PECO:0007241) involving the use of a plant macronutrient or combination of plant macronutrients.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.label: phosphate exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.definition: An inorganic anion exposure (PECO:0001009) involving the application of phosphate (CHEBI:18367).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/COB_00010.label: exposure of organism
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/COB_00010.definition: A process during which an organism comes into contact with another entity.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.label: limited phosphate exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.definition: A phosphate exposure (PECO:0001006) involving exposure to limiting amounts or absence of phosphate (CHEBI:18367).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.label: limited magnesium exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.definition: A magnesium nutrient exposure (PECO:0007288) involving exposure to limiting amounts or the absence of magnesium (CHEBI:25107).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: magnesium nutrient exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: The treatment involving exposure of plant to macronutrient magnesium as supplement to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: potassium exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: The treatment involving exposure of plant to macronutrient potassium as supplement to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.label: limited potassium exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0001.definition: A potassium nutrient exposure (PECO:0007293) involving exposure to limiting amounts or the absence of potassium (CHEBI:26216).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: plant growth medium exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: An abiotic plant exposure (PECO:0007191) involving the use of a solid or liquid substrate for growing plants or tissue-cultured plant samples.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: hydroponic plant culture media exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant growth medium exposure (PECO:0007147) involving growing plants in liquid growth media.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: natural fertilizer exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: Treatment involving the use of organic fertilizer and its component as supplements to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: plant nutrient exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant chemical exposure (PECO:0007189) involving a plant nutrient or a combination of plant nutrients.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: nitrogen exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: Treatment involving the use of nitrogen fertilizer and its components as supplements to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: NPK fertilizer exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: Treatment involving the use of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium supplements to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: abiotic plant exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant exposure (PECO:0001001) involving the application of chemical or non-biological factors.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: fungal plant exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A biotic plant exposure (PECO:0007357) involving exposure of a plant to a fungus or a combination of fungi.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: biotic plant exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A plant exposure (PECO:0001001) involving the application of a biotic or biological factor such as a microbe, insect, animal, or plant or a combination thereof.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: bacterial plant exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: A biotic plant exposure (PECO:0007357) involving exposure of a plant to bacteria.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: phosphorus nutrient exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: The treatment involving exposure of plant to macronutrient phosphorus as supplement to study various types of responses.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.label: root
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.definition: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that lacks shoot axis nodes (PO:0005004) and usually grows indeterminately.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002500.label: cardinal organ part
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002500.definition: A cardinal part of multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025498) that is a proper part of a plant organ (PO:0009008) and includes portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007) of at least two different types.
exact_synonyms: 基本的な（主要な）器官部

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000002.label: root tip
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000002.definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) which is the apical portion of the root (PO:0009005), and includes the root apical meristem (PO:0020147) and root cap (PO:0020123).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002516.label: root epidermal cell
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002516.definition: A plant epidermal cell (PO:0004013) that is part of a root epidermis (PO:0006036).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_00.label: anatomical entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/UBERON_00.definition: Biological entity that is either an individual member of a biological species or constitutes the structural organization of an individual member of a biological species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000025.label: root hair cell
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000025.definition: A root epidermal cell (PO:0025164) that develops from a trichoblast (PO:0000262) and has as part a root hair (GO:0035618).
exact_synonyms: c&#233lula del pelo de la ra&#237z

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000302.label: stolon
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000302.definition: A branch (PO:0025073) that is prostrate or trailing, and produces  adventitious nodal roots (PO:0003005) and sometimes erect shoots.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002507.label: branch
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002507.definition: A shoot axis (PO:00025029) that develops from an axillary bud meristem (PO:0000232) or from equal divisions of a meristematic apical cell (PO:0030007).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002552.label: tuber
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002552.definition: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that is radially enlarged.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000454.label: shoot axis tuber
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000454.definition: A shoot axis (PO:0025029) that develops from a branch (PO:0025073) and is radially enlarged for storage.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002502.label: shoot axis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002502.definition: A plant axis (PO:0025004) that is part of a shoot system (PO:0009006).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000535.label: xylem
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000535.definition: A portion of vascular tissue (PO:0009015) that has as part one or more tracheary elements (PO:0000290).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000901.label: portion of vascular tissue
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000901.definition: A portion of plant tissue (PO:0009007) that has as part one or more tracheary elements (PO:0000290) or sieve elements (PO:0025406).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000541.label: phloem
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000541.definition: A portion of vascular tissue (PO:0009015) that has as parts sieve elements (PO:0025406).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.label: shoot system
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.definition: A collective plant organ structure (PO:0025007) that produces shoot-borne portions of meristem tissue (PO:0009013) and the plant structures (PO:0009011) that arise from them.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002500.label: collective plant organ structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002500.definition: A collective plant structure (PO:0025497) that is a proper part of a whole plant (PO:0000003), and is composed of two or more adjacent plant organs (PO:0009008) and the associated portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.label: multi-tissue plant structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that has as parts two or more portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007) of at least two different types and which through specific morphogenetic processes forms a single structural unit demarcated by primarily bona-fide boundaries from other structural units of different types.
exact_synonyms: 複数の組織からなる植物構造

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.label: plant organ
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.definition: A multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496) that is a functional unit, is a proper part of a whole plant (PO:0000003), and includes portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007) of at least two different types that derive from a common developmental path.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002513.label: plant anatomical entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002513.definition: An anatomical entity that is or was part of a plant.
exact_synonyms: 植物 解剖学（形態）的実体

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000901.label: plant structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000901.definition: A plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) that is, or was, part of a plant, or was derived from a part of a plant.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.label: portion of plant tissue
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000900.definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that consists predominantly of similarly specialized plant cells (PO:0009002) of one or more types.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002012.label: lateral root
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002012.definition: A root (PO:0009005) that develops from a lateral root primordium (PO:0000016) that is part of another root on the same plant.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.label: collective plant structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a proper part of a whole plant (PO:0000003) and includes two or more adjacent plant organs (PO:0009008) or adjacent cardinal organ parts (PO:0025001), along with any associated portions of plant tissue (PO:0009007).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002503.label: leaf
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002503.definition: A phyllome (PO:0006001) that is not associated with a reproductive structure.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000600.label: phyllome
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000600.definition: A lateral plant organ (PO:0009008) produced by a shoot apical meristem (PO:0020148).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: independent continuant
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: b is an independent continuant = Def. b is a continuant which is such that there is no c and no t such that b s-depends_on c at t. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [017-002])

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: p is a process = Def. p is an occurrent that has temporal proper parts and for some time t, p s-depends_on some material entity at t. (axiom label in BFO2 Reference: [083-003])

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000070.label: gene
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000070.definition: A region (or regions) that includes all of the sequence elements necessary to encode a functional transcript. A gene may include regulatory regions, transcribed regions and/or other functional sequence regions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000141.label: biological_region
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000141.definition: A region defined by its disposition to be involved in a biological process.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000000.label: potassium sensitivity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000000.definition: Sensitivity to the potassium ion content in the growth medium. It plays an important role in controlling water by osmosis and also in the metal ion homeostasis.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000024.label: primary macronutrient sensitivity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000024.definition: A macronutrient sensitivity (TO:0000176) response shown by the plant either grown in an excess or deficient amount of the primary macronutrient in the growth medium.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000001.label: nitrogen sensitivity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000001.definition: Sensitivity to the nitrogen content in the growth medium. It is important for protein synthesis, chlorophyll etc.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000004.label: root morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000004.definition: A plant axis morphology trait (TO:0000738) which is a quality of a root (PO:0025025).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.label: plant axis morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.definition: A plant organ morphology trait (TO:0000736) which is a quality of a plant axis (PO:0025004).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.label: root weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the weight of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000035.label: plant dry weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000035.definition: The dry weight of the whole plant.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000007.label: root dry weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000007.definition: The average dry weight of the root determined in a study.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000008.label: root number
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000008.definition: A whole plant morphology trait (TO:0000398) which is the number of roots (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000039.label: whole plant morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000039.definition: A plant structure morphology trait (TO:0000839) which is a quality of a whole plant (PO:0000003).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000010.label: phosphorus response
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000010.definition: Response to the phosphorus content in the growth medium.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000017.label: biotic plant stress trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000017.definition: A plant stress response trait (TO:0000164) which is the response of a plant structure (PO:0009011) to biotic plant stress (PSO:0000011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000011.label: microbial disease response
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000011.definition: A biotic plant stress trait (TO:0000179) which is the response to damage to a plant structure (PO:0009011) caused by an infection by a microbial pathogen.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000011.label: root mass density
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000011.definition: Determined as the dry mass of roots per unit soil volume at a given soil section.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: volumetric density
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A density quality which inheres in a bearer by virtue of some influence exerted by the bearer's mass on a given volume.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000012.label: harvest index
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000012.definition: Proportion of usable (economically significant) biomass over total (biological) biomass, expressed as a percentage.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000037.label: yield trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000037.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is a harvestable product that is a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) or one or more constituent cellular components (GO:0005575) contained therein.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000014.label: relative biomass
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000014.definition: Relative yield was calculated as the ratio of biomass in stress to that of control.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000016.label: plant stress response trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000016.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is the response of a plant structure (PO:0009011) to a plant stress (PSO:0000001).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000016.label: abiotic plant stress response trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000016.definition: A plant stress response trait (TO:0000164) which is the response of a plant structure (PO:0009011) to an abiotic plant stress (PSO:0000012).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000020.label: plant height
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000020.definition: A whole plant morphology trait (TO:0000398) which is the height of a whole plant (PO:0000003).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_100001.label: whole plant size
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_100001.definition: A whole plant morphology trait (TO:0000398) which is the size of a whole plant (PO:0000003).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: height
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A 1-D extent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's vertical dimension of extension.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000022.label: root length
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000022.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the length of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000023.label: root volume
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000023.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the volume of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000017.label: macronutrient response
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000017.definition: A plant nutrient response trait (TO:0000480) shown by the plant grown in either an excess or deficient amount of the macronutrient in the growth medium.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000038.label: plant trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000038.definition: A measurable or observable characteristic of a cellular component (GO:0005575), biological process (GO:0008150) or molecular function (GO:0003674) that is part of, or has participant a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) and/or a plant structure development stage (PO:0009012).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000025.label: plant vigor trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000025.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is a measure of the active and/or healthy growth and development of a plant stucture (PO:0009011) or a population of plants.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: branched
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A branchiness quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having branches.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000271.label: root shape
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000271.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the shape of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000025.label: root branching
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000025.definition: The extent of the root branching as determined under variable treatments and environments.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.label: biochemical trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is a quality of a chemical entity (CHEBI:24431), a plant metabolite (CHEBI:76924), or a molecular function (GO:0003674), which occurs in a cellular component (GO:0005575), plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) or during a plant structure development stage (PO:0009012).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.label: root length to shoot length ratio
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000027.definition: The ratio determined from the parameters evaluated for root length and the shoot length in a study.
exact_synonyms: root length to shoot length ratio

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.label: stem length
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.definition: A stem morphology trait (TO:0000361) which is the length of the stem (PO:0009047).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000028.label: metabolite content trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000028.definition: A biochemical trait (TO:0000277) which is the amount of a metabolite in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000029.label: carbohydrate content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000029.definition: A metabolite content trait (TO:0000281) which is the amount of carbohydrate (CHEBI:16646) in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000030.label: root thickness
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000030.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the thickness of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000032.label: shoot system yield trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000032.definition: A yield trait (TO: 0000371) that is the amount of a plant structure (PO:0009011) or portion of plant substance (PO:0025161) produced by the shoot system (PO:0009006) which is harvested.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000032.label: sucrose content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000032.definition: The amount of sucrose present in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000600.label: oligosaccharide content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000600.definition: Amount of oligosaccharides present in the plant or its parts.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000033.label: sugar content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000033.definition: Amount of sugar present in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000034.label: total soluble sugar content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000034.definition: Total amount of soluble sugar present in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.label: leaf elongation rate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.definition: Measure of growth or elongation rate of the leaf in a plant.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000065.label: leaf growth and development trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000065.definition: A plant organ development trait (TO:0000927) that has as primary participant a leaf (PO:0025034).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.label: shoot system elongation rate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.definition: A shoot system growth and development trait (TO:0000654) which is the rate of growth of the shoot system.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000065.label: shoot system growth and development trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000065.definition: A plant structure growth and development trait (TO:0000928) that is a quality of the growth of the shoot system (PO:0009006), and shoot system development stages (PO:0025527).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000083.label: plant structure morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000083.definition: A plant morphology trait (TO:0000017) which is a quality of a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000045.label: biomass yield
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000045.definition: A yield trait (TO:0000371) which is the amount of biomass obtained.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000046.label: mineral and ion content trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000046.definition: A biochemical trait (TO:0000277) that is the amount of a particular mineral or ion constituent occurring in a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000048.label: plant nutrient response trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000048.definition: A biochemical response trait (TO:0000277) which is the plant's response to an excess or deficient amount of the nutrients in the growth environment.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000028.label: biological process trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000028.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is a process quality (PATO:0001236) of a biological process (GO:0008150) which occurs in a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131), a cellular component (GO:0005575), or during a plant structure development stage (PO:0009012).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000050.label: nitrogen recycling
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000050.definition: It is a measure of reduced net ammonium production in response to the receipt of photosynthate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.label: mineral and ion transport trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.definition: A biological process trait (TO:0000283) which is associated with directed movement of minerals and ions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.label: phosphorus uptake
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.definition: A mineral and ion transport trait (TO:0020096) which involves phosphorus ion uptake in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.label: potassium uptake
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.definition: A mineral and ion transport trait (TO:0020096) which involves potassium ion uptake in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.label: relative growth rate
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000051.definition: A plant vigor trait (TO:0000250) that is the increase in aboveground biomass in a defined period of time.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000055.label: shoot dry weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000055.definition: The dry weight of the shoot without inflorescence.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000056.label: shoot axis weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000056.definition: A shoot axis morphology trait (TO:0000739) which is the weight of a shoot axis.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.label: shoot axis morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.definition: A plant axis morphology trait (TO:0000738) which is a quality of a shoot axis (PO:0025029).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.label: shoot fresh weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.definition: Fresh weight of the shoot without inflorescence.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000089.label: stem size
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000089.definition: A stem morphology trait (TO:0000361) which is the size of a stem (PO:0009047).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.label: root fresh weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000057.definition: The average fresh weight of the root determined in a study.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000060.label: potassium content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000060.definition: A mineral and ion content trait (TO:0000465) which is the potassium cation (CHEBI:29103) composition in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: composition
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A single physical entity inhering in an bearer by virtue of the bearer's quantities or relative ratios of subparts.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000092.label: plant structure growth and development trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000092.definition: A plant growth and development trait (TO:0000357) which is a quality of a plant structure development stage (PO:0009028).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000600.label: polysaccharide content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000600.definition: Amount of polysaccharide present in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000069.label: starch content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000069.definition: Amount of starch present in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000059.label: enzyme activity trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000059.definition: A biochemical trait which is a quality of an enzymatic reaction.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000070.label: phosphatase activity trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000070.definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of phosphoric monoesters, releasing inorganic phosphate.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: characteristic
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: The properties, attributes, or modifiers used to describe an entity or process or some aspect of an entity or process.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000083.label: multi-tissue plant structure morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000083.definition: A plant structure morphology trait (TO:0000839) which is a quality of a multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.label: plant organ morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000073.definition: A multi-tissue plant structure morphology trait (TO:0000836) which is a quality of a plant organ (PO:0009008).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000084.label: collective plant organ structure morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000084.definition: A collective plant structure morphology trait (TO:0000840) which is a quality of a collective plant organ structure (PO:0025007).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000084.label: collective plant structure morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000084.definition: A plant structure morphology trait (TO:0000839) which is a quality of a collective plant structure (PO:0025497).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000035.label: plant growth and development trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000035.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is the growth (GO:0048590) and development (GO:0032502) of a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) or a constituent cellular component (GO:0005575).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000098.label: root system morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000098.definition: A collective plant organ structure morphology trait (TO:0000842) which is a quality of a root system (PO:0025025).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000101.label: lateral root length
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000101.definition: A root length (TO:0000227) that is the length of one or more lateral roots (PO:0020121).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000104.label: root yield
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000104.definition: A yield trait (TO:0000371) which is the yield of roots (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000102.label: phosphorus content

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: mass density

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000105.label: root hair density
