http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000105.label: root cross sectional area
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000105.definition: A root morphology trait (TO:0000043) which is the cross sectional area of a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000107.label: shoot axis tuber yield
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000107.definition: A shoot system yield trait (TO:0000327) which is the yield of shoot axis tubers (PO:0004543).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_100004.label: root system phosphorus content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_100004.definition: A phosphorus content trait (TO:0001024) which is the phosphorus cation (CHEBI:33467) composition in a root system (PO:0025025).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000112.label: root phosphorus content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000112.definition: A phosphorus content trait (TO:0001024) which is the phosphorus cation (CHEBI:33467) composition in a root (PO:0009005).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000266.label: root hair length

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.label: plant cell length

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000047.label: growth hormone content

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000267.label: auxin content

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000074.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber mass
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000074.definition: A subterranean shoot axis tuber morphology trait (TO:0000742) which is the mass of a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000301.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber fresh weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000301.definition: A subterranean shoot axis tuber weight trait (TO:0000746) which is the fresh weight of a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000301.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber dry weight
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000301.definition: A subterranean shoot axis tuber weight trait (TO:0000746) which is the dry weight of a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000306.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber nitrogen content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000306.definition: A nitrogen content trait (TO:0020093) which is the amount of nitrogen (CHEBI:51143) in a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.label: nitrogen content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.definition: A mineral and ion content trait (TO:0000465) which is the amount of nitrogen (CHEBI:51143) in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000308.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber phosphorus content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000308.definition: A phosphorus content trait (TO:0001024) which is the amount of phosphorus cation (CHEBI:33467) in a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000604.label: phosphorus concentration
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000604.definition: A phosphorus content (TO:0001024) which is the concentration of phosphorus (CHEBI:26082) in some plant structure (PO:0009011)

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002008.label: stover nitrogen content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002008.definition: A trait to measure percent nitrogen concentration in the stover sample used for predicting crude protein (CP) content of stover by multiplication with a factor of 6.25 (CP = N x 6.25). This concentration is one of the criteria to assess the quality of fodder. Value derived from the analysis of stover using Near Infrared Reflectance Spectrophotometry (NIRS).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.label: nitrate content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002009.definition: A mineral and ion content trait (TO:0000465) which is the amount of nitrate (CHEBI:17632) in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.label: nitrate uptake
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.definition: A mineral and ion transport trait (TO:0020096) which involves nitrate ion uptake in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.label: phosphate content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.definition: A mineral and ion content trait (TO:0000465) which is the amount of phosphate (CHEBI:26020) in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.label: adventitious root length
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.definition: A root length (TO:0000227) trait which is the length of an adventitious root (shoot-borne root; PO:0000042).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.label: Indole-3-acetic acid content
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_002010.definition: An auxin content (TO:0002672) which is the amount of indole-3-acetic acid (CHEBI:16411) in a plant structure (PO:0009011).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.label: main group molecular entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.definition: A molecular entity containing one or more atoms from any of groups 1, 2, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 of the periodic table.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.label: main group element atom
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.definition: An atom belonging to one of the main groups (found in the s- and p- blocks) of the periodic table.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.label: metal atom
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.definition: An atom of an element that exhibits typical metallic properties, being typically shiny, with high electrical and thermal conductivity.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_362.label: disaccharide
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_362.definition: A compound in which two monosaccharides are joined by a glycosidic bond.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_487.label: agonist
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_487.definition: Substance which binds to cell receptors normally responding to naturally occurring substances and which produces a response of its own.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_248.label: indol-3-yl carboxylic acid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_248.definition: Any indolyl carboxylic acid carrying an indol-3-yl or substituted indol-3-yl group.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_225.label: anion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_225.definition: A monoatomic or polyatomic species having one or more elementary charges of the electron.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.label: carboxylic acid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.definition: A carbon oxoacid acid carrying at least one ‒C(=O)OH group and having the structure RC(=O)OH, where R is any any monovalent functional group. Carboxylic acids are the most common type of organic acid.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: atom
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: A chemical entity constituting the smallest component of an element having the chemical properties of the element.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.label: pnictogen molecular entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_333.definition: A p-block molecular entity containing any pnictogen.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_393.label: growth regulator
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_393.definition: Any chemical substance that inhibits the life-cycle of an organism.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_508.label: organic molecular entity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_508.definition: Any molecular entity that contains carbon.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.label: application
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_332.definition: Intended use of the molecular entity or part thereof by humans.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.label: p-block element atom
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_335.definition: Any main group element atom belonging to the p-block of the periodic table.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_354.label: oxoanion
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_354.definition: An oxoanion is an anion derived from an oxoacid by loss of hydron(s) bound to oxygen.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_371.label: homopolysaccharide
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_371.definition: Glycans composed of a single type of monosaccharide residue. They are named by replacing the ending '-ose' of the sugar by '-an'.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_336.label: hydrides
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_336.definition: Hydrides are chemical compounds of hydrogen with other chemical elements.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_244.label: biological role
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_244.definition: A role played by the molecular entity or part thereof within a biological context.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_334.label: phosphorus oxoacid
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_334.definition: A pnictogen oxoacid which contains phosphorus and oxygen, at least one hydrogen atom bound to oxygen, and forms an ion by the loss of one or more protons.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_167.label: glycan
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_167.definition: Any oligosaccharide, polysaccharide or their derivatives consisting of monosaccharides or monosaccharide derivatives linked by glycosidic bonds. See also http://www.ontobee.org/ontology/GNO?iri=http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GNO_00000001.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_632.label: carbohydrate derivative
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_632.definition: Any organooxygen compound derived from a carbohydrate by replacement of one or more hydroxy group(s) by an amino group, a thiol group or similar heteroatomic groups. The term also includes derivatives of these compounds.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_522.label: physiological role
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_522.definition: A biological role relating to the normal mechanisms and their interactions within a living system.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_369.label: organooxygen compound
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/CHEBI_369.definition: An organochalcogen compound containing at least one carbon-oxygen bond.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000257.label: system
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000257.definition: A material entity consisting of multiple components that are causally integrated.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005117.label: localization
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_005117.definition: Any process in which a cell, a substance, or a cellular entity, such as a protein complex or organelle, is transported, tethered to or otherwise maintained in a specific location. In the case of substances, localization may also be achieved via selective degradation.
narrow_synonyms: establishment and maintenance of cellular component location
establishment and maintenance of substance location
establishment and maintenance of substrate location

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004317.label: macromolecule metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004317.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving macromolecules, any molecule of high relative molecular mass, the structure of which essentially comprises the multiple repetition of units derived, actually or conceptually, from molecules of low relative molecular mass.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000905.label: biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000905.definition: A cellular process consisting of the biochemical pathways by which a living organism synthesizes chemical substances. This typically represents the energy-requiring part of metabolism in which simpler substances are transformed into more complex ones.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003166.label: cellular response to nutrient levels
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003166.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus reflecting the presence, absence, or concentration of nutrients.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003355.label: cellular response to stress
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003355.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating the organism is under stress. The stress is usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004885.label: anatomical structure development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004885.definition: The biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of an anatomical structure from an initial condition to its mature state. This process begins with the formation of the structure and ends with the mature structure, whatever form that may be including its natural destruction. An anatomical structure is any biological entity that occupies space and is distinguished from its surroundings. Anatomical structures can be macroscopic such as a carpel, or microscopic such as an acrosome.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003250.label: developmental process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003250.definition: A biological process whose specific outcome is the progression of an integrated living unit: an anatomical structure (which may be a subcellular structure, cell, tissue, or organ), or organism over time from an initial condition to a later condition.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000985.label: auxin metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000985.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving auxins, a group of plant hormones that regulate aspects of plant growth.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004244.label: hormone biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004244.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of any hormone, naturally occurring substances secreted by specialized cells that affects the metabolism or behavior of other cells possessing functional receptors for the hormone.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002280.label: passive transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002280.definition: Enables the transfer of a single solute from one side of a membrane to the other by a mechanism involving conformational change, either by facilitated diffusion or in a membrane potential dependent process if the solute is charged.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002280.label: active transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_002280.definition: Enables the transfer of a specific substance or related group of substances from one side of a membrane to the other, up the solute's concentration gradient. The transporter binds the solute and undergoes a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001577.label: oligosaccharide transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001577.definition: The directed movement of oligosaccharides into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Oligosaccharides are molecules with between two and (about) 20 monosaccharide residues connected by glycosidic linkages.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000521.label: transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000521.definition: Enables the directed movement of substances (such as macromolecules, small molecules, ions) into, out of or within a cell, accross or in between cells.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.label: monoatomic cation transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000681.definition: The directed movement of a monoatomic cation, into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Monatomic cations (also called simple cations) are positively charged ions consisting of exactly one atom.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004858.label: developmental growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004858.definition: The increase in size or mass of an entire organism, a part of an organism or a cell, where the increase in size or mass has the specific outcome of the progression of the organism over time from one condition to another.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_200105.label: reactive nitrogen species metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_200105.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving a reactive nitrogen species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004343.label: oxoacid metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004343.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving any oxoacid; an oxoacid is a compound which contains oxygen, at least one other element, and at least one hydrogen bound to oxygen, and which produces a conjugate base by loss of positive hydrogen ion(s) (hydrons).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004243.label: indole-containing compound metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004243.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving compounds that contain an indole (2,3-benzopyrrole) skeleton.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001678.label: hydrolase activity, acting on ester bonds
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001678.definition: Catalysis of the hydrolysis of any ester bond.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000695.label: response to stress
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000695.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a disturbance in organismal or cellular homeostasis, usually, but not necessarily, exogenous (e.g. temperature, humidity, ionizing radiation).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001539.label: primary active transmembrane transporter activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001539.definition: Enables the transfer of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other, up the solute's concentration gradient, by binding the solute and undergoing a series of conformational changes. Transport works equally well in either direction and is powered by a primary energy source. Primary energy sources known to be coupled to transport are chemical such as ATP hydrolysis, redox energy and photon energy.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_014065.label: ATP-dependent activity
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_014065.definition: A molecular function characterized by the coupling of ATP hydrolysis to other steps of a reaction mechanism to make the reaction energetically favorable, for example to catalyze a reaction or drive transport against a concentration gradient.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009069.label: post-embryonic plant organ development
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009069.definition: Development, taking place during the post-embryonic phase of a plant tissue or tissues that work together to perform a specific function or functions. Development pertains to the process whose specific outcome is the progression of a structure over time, from its formation to the mature structure. Organs are commonly observed as visibly distinct structures, but may also exist as loosely associated clusters of cells that work together to perform a specific function or functions.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001604.label: cell growth
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_001604.definition: The process in which a cell irreversibly increases in size over time by accretion and biosynthetic production of matter similar to that already present.
related_synonyms: metabolic process resulting in cell growth
non-developmental growth of a unicellular organism

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003287.label: regulation of localization
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003287.definition: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of any process in which a cell, a substance, or a cellular entity is transported to, or maintained in, a specific location.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000991.label: hormone transport
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_000991.definition: The directed movement of hormones into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003278.label: monocarboxylic acid metabolic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_003278.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways involving monocarboxylic acids, any organic acid containing one carboxyl (COOH) group or anion (COO-).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004639.label: carboxylic acid biosynthetic process
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004639.definition: The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of carboxylic acids, any organic acid containing one or more carboxyl (-COOH) groups.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004887.label: chemical homeostasis
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004887.definition: Any biological process involved in the maintenance of an internal steady state of a chemical.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004299.label: cell projection
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004299.definition: A prolongation or process extending from a cell, e.g. a flagellum or axon.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004222.label: response to chemical
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_004222.definition: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a chemical stimulus.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_199035.label: transporter complex
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_199035.definition: A protein complex facilitating transport of molecules (proteins, small molecules, nucleic acids) into, out of or within a cell, or between cells.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009879.label: membrane protein complex
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GO_009879.definition: Any protein complex that is part of a membrane.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0002.label: branchiness
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0002.definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the degree to which there are subdivisions or offshoots in a bearer entity.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.label: multi-species collection of organisms
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PCO_00000.definition: A collection of organisms that consists of two or more organisms from at least two species.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: chemical exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: An abiotic plant exposure (PECO:0007191) involving the application of chemical(s).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.label: secondary macronutrient exposure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PECO_0007.definition: An exposure involving the use of macronutrients (Ca, Mg, S) as supplement to study various types of responses. These macronutrients are used less often as fertilizers than the primary elements.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.label: cardinal part of multi-tissue plant structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_002549.definition: A plant structure (PO:0009011) that is a proper part of a multi-tissue plant structure (PO:0025496) and includes portions of plant tissues (PO:0009007) of at least two different types.
exact_synonyms: parte cardinal de estructura vegetal con m&#250ltiples tejidos
複数の組織からなる植物構造の基本（主要）部分

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000401.label: plant epidermal cell
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PO_000401.definition: A native plant cell (PO:0025606) that is part of a portion of epidermis (PO:0005679).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000000.label: region
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/SO_000000.definition: A sequence_feature with an extent greater than zero. A nucleotide region is composed of bases and a polypeptide region is composed of amino acids.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.label: process characteristic
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0001.definition: A characteristic which inheres in a process.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000092.label: plant organ growth and development trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000092.definition: A multi-tissue plant structure development trait (TO:0000927) that has as primary participant a plant organ (PO:0009008).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000074.label: subterranean shoot axis tuber morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000074.definition: A tuber morphology trait (TO:0000741) which is a quality of a subterranean shoot axis tuber (PO:0004547).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000001.label: plant morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000001.definition: A plant trait (TO:0000387) which is a morphological quality of a plant anatomical entity (PO:0025131) or a constituent cellular component (GO:0005575) contained therein.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.label: stem morphology trait
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000036.definition: A shoot axis morphology trait (TO:0000739) which is the quality of a stem (PO:0009047).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.label: shape
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/PATO_0000.definition: A morphological quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's ratios of distances between its features (points, edges, surfaces and also holes etc).

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000268.label: plant cell size
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000268.definition: A plant cell morphology trait (TO:0002683) which is the size of a plant cell (PO:0009002) type.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/TO_000092.label: multi-tissue plant structure growth and development trait

urn:soil-crop-health:ScientificAssertion.label: scientific assertion
urn:soil-crop-health:ScientificAssertion.definition: A source-bounded, evidence-linked assertion extracted from a scientific document; not a context-free universal fact.

NMDC Soil local scale value set
NMDC PlantAssociated environmental medium value set

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: has part
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: a core relation that holds between a whole and its part

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: part of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: a core relation that holds between a part and its whole

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000008.label: has quality
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000008.definition: a relation between an independent continuant (the bearer) and a quality, in which the quality specifically depends on the bearer for its existence

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000213.label: overlaps
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000213.definition: x overlaps y if and only if there exists some z such that x has part z and z part of y

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.label: characteristic of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.definition: a relation between a specifically dependent continuant (the characteristic) and any other entity (the bearer), in which the characteristic depends on the bearer for its existence.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.label: regulates
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.definition: p regulates q iff p is causally upstream of q, the execution of p is not constant and varies according to specific conditions, and p influences the rate or magnitude of execution of q due to an effect either on some enabler of q or some enabler of a part of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.label: participates in
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.definition: a relation between a continuant and a process, in which the continuant is somehow involved in the process

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000231.label: characteristic of part of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000231.definition: q characteristic of part of w if and only if there exists some p such that q inheres in p and p part of w.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.label: has participant
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000005.definition: a relation between a process and a continuant, in which the continuant is somehow involved in the process

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000102.label: located in
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000102.definition: a relation between two independent continuants, the target and the location, in which the target is entirely within the location

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000231.label: transports or maintains localization of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000231.definition: Holds between p and c when p is a localization process (localization covers maintenance of localization as well as its establishment)  and the outcome of this process is to regulate the localization of c.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000202.label: transports
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000202.definition: Holds between p and c when p is a transport process or transporter activity and the outcome of this p is to move c from one location to another.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000300.label: produces
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000300.definition: a produces b if some process that occurs_in a has_output b, where a and b are material entities. Examples: hybridoma cell line produces monoclonal antibody reagent; chondroblast produces avascular GAG-rich matrix.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000216.label: in taxon
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000216.definition: x is in taxon y if an only if y is an organism, and the relationship between x and y is one of: part of (reflexive), developmentally preceded by, derives from, secreted by, expressed.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000232.label: evolutionarily related to
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000232.definition: A relationship that holds via some environmental process

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.label: causally upstream of
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.definition: p is causally upstream of q iff p is causally related to q, the end of p precedes the end of q, and p is not an occurrent part of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.label: negatively regulates
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.definition: p negatively regulates q iff p regulates q, and p decreases the rate or magnitude of execution of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000230.label: causally upstream of, negative effect
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000230.definition: p is causally upstream of, negative effect q iff p is casually upstream of q, and the execution of p decreases the execution of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.label: positively regulates
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000221.definition: p positively regulates q iff p regulates q, and p increases the rate or magnitude of execution of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000230.label: causally upstream of, positive effect
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000230.definition: p is causally upstream of, positive effect q iff p is casually upstream of q, and the execution of p is required for the execution of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000223.label: has input
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000223.definition: p has input c iff: p is a process, c is a material entity, c is a participant in p, c is present at the start of p, and the state of c is modified during p.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000223.label: has output
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000223.definition: p has output c iff c is a participant in p, c is present at the end of p, and c is not present in the same state at the beginning of p.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000404.label: causally upstream of or within, positive effect
causally upstream of or within, negative effect

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.label: causally related to
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.definition: relation that links two events, processes, states, or objects such that one event, process, state, or object (a cause) contributes to the production of another event, process, state, or object (an effect) where the cause is partly or wholly responsible for the effect, and the effect is partly or wholly dependent on the cause.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.label: causally upstream of or within
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000241.definition: p is 'causally upstream or within' q iff p is causally related to q, and the end of p precedes, or is coincident with, the end of q.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.label: precedes
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/BFO_00000.definition: x precedes y if and only if the time point at which x ends is before or equivalent to the time point at which y starts. Formally: x precedes y iff ω(x) <= α(y), where α is a function that maps a process to a start point, and ω is a function that maps a process to an end point.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000261.label: correlated with
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000261.definition: A relationship that holds between two entities, where the entities exhibit a statistical dependence relationship. The entities may be statistical variables, or they may be other kinds of entities such as diseases, chemical entities or processes.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000222.label: temporally related to
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000222.definition: A relation that holds between two occurrents. This is a grouping relation that collects together all the Allen relations.

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000232.label: mereotopologically related to
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000232.definition: A mereological relationship or a topological relationship

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_004003.label: results in changes to anatomical or cellular structure
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_004003.definition: p has anatomical participant c iff p has participant c, and c is an anatomical entity

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000233.label: related via localization to
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000233.definition: A relationship that holds via some process of localization

http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000250.label: causal relation between processes
http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/RO_000250.definition: p is causally related to q if and only if p or any part of p and q or any part of q are linked by a chain of events where each event pair is one where the execution of p influences the execution of q. p may be upstream, downstream, part of, or a container of q.

urn:soil-crop-health:originalRelation.definition: Surface predicate phrase extracted from the source sentence prior to ontology property mapping.

urn:soil-crop-health:numericValue.label: numeric value
urn:soil-crop-health:numericValue.definition: A numeric value reported for a measurement, treatment level or effect size in the cited assertion.

urn:soil-crop-health:certainty.label: source certainty
urn:soil-crop-health:certainty.definition: Reported modality or epistemic certainty of the assertion in the source text.

urn:soil-crop-health:sourceDocument.label: source document
urn:soil-crop-health:sourceDocument.definition: Document key or DOI identifying the source paper.

urn:soil-crop-health:sourceText.label: source evidence text
urn:soil-crop-health:sourceText.definition: Verbatim text span from the source document supporting the assertion.

urn:soil-crop-health:sourcePage.label: source page
urn:soil-crop-health:sourcePage.definition: Page number in the source document where the assertion appears.

urn:soil-crop-health:unitText.label: unit text
urn:soil-crop-health:unitText.definition: Literal unit string reported with a measurement or treatment level.

urn:soil-crop-health:citationText.label: citation text
urn:soil-crop-health:citationText.definition: Bibliographic citation string associated with the assertion.

urn:soil-crop-health:qualifiers.label: assertion qualifiers
urn:soil-crop-health:qualifiers.definition: Structured experimental, anatomical, temporal, or cultivar qualifiers bounding an assertion.
